one_liner: MIT texture-compression kernels (BC1-7, ETC1/2) whose scalar BC6H decoder narrowly beat bcdec in aras-p's 2022 single-thread test.
what_it_does: Stand-alone kernels from Convection Texture Tools: encoders for BC1-BC7, ETC1, ETC2 (RGB, RGBA, punchthrough) and 11-bit EAC, plus decoders for BC6H (unsigned and signed) and BC7 only. The public API (cvtt::Kernels::EncodeBC7, DecodeBC6HU, DecodeBC6HS, DecodeBC7, ...) always takes exactly cvtt::NumParallelBlocks = 8 4x4 blocks per call through PixelBlockU8 or PixelBlockF16 structs (BC6H pixels are half-float bit patterns stored in int16_t), so callers pad partial batches. There is no image-level, DDS or KTX API and no float32 output; the benchmark called the internal per-block cvtt::Internal::BC6HComputer::UnpackOne, which the public Decode functions loop over.
how_it_is_fast: The BC6H decoder loads the 128-bit block into four 32-bit words, shifts the 65- or 82-bit header out in one step, and runs a per-mode generated straight-line function (BC6H_IO g_readFuncs, one for each of the 14 modes) that gathers the scattered endpoint bits with constant masks and shifts, instead of walking a per-bit mode-descriptor table as the DirectXTex-derived layout does. Endpoints are then sign-extended, delta-decoded and unquantised in integer math, and the 16 pixels are interpolated with the BC6H weight tables; the decoder is plain scalar C++, so the gain comes from cheap bit extraction, not SIMD. The encoders (not part of the measured claim) use an SPMD design that processes 8 blocks per call with SSE2 16-bit math through ParallelMath, with a scalar fallback elsewhere.
when_to_use: Bulk CPU decoding of BC6H (HDR) textures on x86-64 or Apple Silicon, single-threaded, where 1.0-1.2x over bcdec is worth an extra dependency (aras-p measured 101-149 Mpix/s).
You already vendor CVTT for BC6H, BC7 or ETC encoding (Godot ships it as thirdparty/cvtt) and want the matching decoder for round-trip error measurement.
You want BC6H output as half floats: UnpackOne writes FP16 bit patterns directly, so no float32 round trip is needed if the consumer takes FP16.
One MIT library covering both encode and decode of BC6H and BC7.
when_not_to_use: BC1-BC5 decoding: there are no decoders for them; use bcdec (every BCn format in one header) or etcpak (fastest BC1/BC3 in the same test).
BC7 decoding: slower than bcdec (124 vs 142 Mpix/s with VS2022, 121 vs 169 with clang 14) and 4-5x slower than bc7enc_rdo's bc7decomp (621 and 656 Mpix/s).
Where the margin must hold up: with clang 14 it ties bcdec (105 vs 104 Mpix/s), and bcdec has moved on since the measured e3ca0 while this repo has not changed since 2022-06-23.
Small builds: aras-p counts 9 source files and 487 KB of source to get two decoders, mostly encoder code; bcdec is one 69 KB header.
Projects that need maintained code: the README still labels BC6H 'Experimental' and the project has had no commits since 2022.

integration.form: source-drop / static lib (10 .cpp and 23 .h files; ConvectionKernels_SingleFile.cpp with CVTT_SINGLE_FILE builds everything as one translation unit; a Visual Studio project is included, no CMake)
integration.dependencies: none beyond the C/C++ standard headers (emmintrin.h when SSE2 is enabled)
integration.min_toolchain: C++ without a documented standard; aras-p built it as C++17 with Visual Studio 2022, clang 14 (clang-cl) and Apple clang 13
integration.platforms: any; SSE2 SIMD on x86/x64 (CVTT_USE_SSE2 is defined automatically when SSE2 is available), scalar ParallelMath elsewhere including ARM64 (no NEON path); the decoders are scalar on every platform
integration.thread_safety: not documented for the decoders; from the code they keep all state on the stack and read const tables, so concurrent calls on different blocks look safe; the README says ETC encoder scratch data may move between threads but must not be used by two encode calls at once
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: false - not a bcdec or DirectXTex replacement: it decodes only BC6H and BC7, in fixed batches of 8 blocks into PixelBlockF16/PixelBlockU8 structs that the caller must scatter into the image

gotchas: Public DecodeBC6HU/DecodeBC6HS/DecodeBC7 always read 8 blocks (128 bytes) and write 8 output blocks; decoding a single block or an image whose block count is not a multiple of 8 needs padded buffers, or the cvtt::Internal::...::UnpackOne functions from ConvectionKernels_BC67.h that the benchmark used (not in the public header).

The BC6H decoder was broken until the day of the measurement: aras-p's issue #6 (2022-06-22) reported that UnpackOne produced 'something entirely else', and commit 350416d 'Fix bit framing error in BC6H decoder' (2022-06-23) fixed it; that commit is the one benchmarked and the last in the repo. Any copy taken from an older commit decodes BC6H incorrectly.

Godot's thirdparty/cvtt (pinned at 350416d) still applies 0001-revert-bc6h-reorg.patch from PR #73715 (February 2023, a BC6H quality-regression fix), which swaps the generated per-mode BC6H read/write code, including inside UnpackOne, back to the older per-bit mode-descriptor tables. Copies taken from Godot therefore do not contain the decoder that was measured.

Reserved or invalid BC6H mode bits decode silently to black with alpha 1.0, with no error return; the harness's output-hash check only prints a warning on mismatch, so bit-exactness of the timed output rests on the post's statement that only Compressonator differed on BC6H.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ConvectionKernels only for BC6H decode throughput, or when you already ship its BC6H/BC7/ETC encoders; otherwise bcdec covers every BCn format in one header and tied or nearly tied it on BC6H, and bc7enc_rdo's bc7decomp (bc7enc family) is 4-5x faster on BC7. For BC7 encoding, bc7e and bc7enc have independent quality and speed measurements; CVTT's encoders have none in this catalogue.
verified_claims_summary: aras-p's public bcn_decoder_tester (20 runs per DDS file, one thread, every BC6H decoder producing float32 RGB, Windows builds RelWithDebInfo plus /Ob2) measured ConvectionKernels 350416d's BC6H unsigned decoder at 101 Mpix/s against bcdec e3ca0's 85 (1.19x) with VS2022 and 105 against 104 (a tie) with clang 14 on a Ryzen 5950X, and at 149 against SwiftShader's 143 and bcdec's 79 on an Apple M1 Max with Apple clang 13; DirectXTex was 3-4x slower, and on BC7 it trailed both bcdec and bc7enc_rdo.
status_note: Abandoned since 2022-06-23 (the BC6H bit-framing fix that was benchmarked); MIT-licensed with a DirectXTex-derived notice, 53 stars, and vendored by Godot at that commit but with the BC6H reorganisation reverted. Copyable, but treat BC6H as the README does: experimental.
